summary:
Bullpen is the category to lean on across the board today — R1, R2, and R3 are all riding 3-game winning streaks on bullpen ratings, sitting at 100-90 (53%) over the last 14 days versus a flat 50% season baseline. That's the one stat that's actually moving right now, and it's live in exactly the kind of low-scoring, pen-dependent games on tonight's board. Meanwhile sp is the fade: R3's starting-pitcher category is flagged cold at -5.2pts, and across all three live ratings sp sits at just 86-104 (45%) over 14 days. Runs is also souring for R2, a 4-game losing streak at 89-101 (47%) recently against a 52% season number — worth discounting if R2's edge in a game is runs-driven rather than bullpen-driven.

On today's slate, all four ratings are in lockstep on five of nine games — STL@CIN (fading STL hard, -2.00 to -2.06), SEA@MIL (+1.31 to +2.27 on MIL), WSN@TEX, TOR@TBR, and NYY@BAL — and that kind of unanimous consensus across R1-R3 (R4 has no track record yet, so treat its votes as confirmation only) is where you want size. TBR is the standout team-side play here: model backing at TBR shows 25-10 (71%) on picks and a blistering 18-5 (78%, +22.0u) on strong plays, and tonight's game has the biggest ratings agreement on the board (+0.48 to +1.29 across R1-R3) with Bieber facing Seymour — exactly the profile where a hot bullpen signal and a proven team-when-liked leader stack. MIL is another green light — 25-15 (62%) on picks, 14-8 strong — backing the big SEA@MIL number. The one crack in the board is ATL@CHW, where R3 flips to ATL (-0.20) while R1/R2/R4 like CHW; skip or minimize that one given R3's cold sp signal is likely the driver of the split. HOU is the one team to treat carefully even with a small CONSENSUS lean (+0.43 to +0.88) — strong-play record there is ugly at 3-8 (27%, -8.0u), so don't let today's mild lean turn into a full-unit play.
